Senses.Explanation: (兼) both / holding-together / combining + (中) within, amid + (到) arrive, reach: "arrival within both." It is the last of the Five Ranks (五位) that Dongshan Liangjie composed as the (五位君臣頌) in his own record — (正中偏) · (偏中正) · (正中來) · (兼中至) · (兼中到) — his verse-line being (兼中到)。(不落有無誰敢和)。(人人盡欲出常流)。(折合還歸炭裏坐) (T47n1986B); the closing image "...fold back and return to sit in the charcoal" (折合還歸炭裏坐) is quoted 24 times across 20 texts. In the corpus it is deployed as a fixed catechism-question — (如何是兼中到) occurs 104 times in 57 texts, each master capping it (師曰。撥開雲外路。脫去月明前; 崑崙夜裏行; 十道不通耗; and so on) — and as a lemma the commentators define. Their self-definitions: "substance and function, thus-and-thus, is arrival within both," (體用如如為兼中到 X73n1457); "...the utmost of reaching the Way, principle and phenomena both extinguished," (此即兼中到也。造道之極，理事俱泯 X72n1437); and it is placed opposite the 4th rank by a (功)／(位) (merit/position) contrast — "(兼中至) is set where merit and position are both manifest, (兼中到) where both are extinguished," (兼中至，約功位雙彰時立，兼中到，約功位雙泯時立 X72n1441); the phrase (功位俱隱), which X72n1437 ties to this rank (兼中到，就功位俱隱時立), recurs 27 times across the corpus — though most of those (19 of 27) sit in the distinct (功勳) four-question catechism (轉功就位／功位齊彰／轉位就功／功位俱隱) that carries no explicit (兼中到) label. As with (正中來), one (五燈全書) (上堂) maps a single shout onto the ranks — (我此一喝)，(聖凡情盡)，(能所兩忘)，(妙盡有無)，(是兼中到也) — and in its Linji-school restatement says (兼中到)，(即元要妙旨也) (X82n1571). The graphs read alike across witnesses; the term carries no gloss here beyond its literal reading and its terminal place in Dongshan's set.
Senses.Note: Corpus-wide sense (SenseKey null): 276 occurrences in 84 allowlist texts. (Counts are whole-file, tag-stripped with <note>/<rdg>/<orig> apparatus excluded; gate-2 recount, confirmed by two independent recounts.) The source verse is Dongshan Liangjie's own (T47n1986B, 師。作五位君臣頌云…) — attributed to him; the remaining curated items are the fixed (如何是兼中到) catechism and later Caodong analytical prose, narrated/raised, MasterName null. VARIANT (the 至/到 question): (兼中到) (到 = arrive/reach) is the FIFTH and terminal rank and is stable across the corpus; it is distinguished from the 4th rank (兼中至) (至 = arrive) not by graph-sense — (到) and (至) are near-synonyms — but by the (功位雙泯) (both extinguished) vs (功位雙彰) (both manifest) contrast the texts draw (X72n1441). The real cross-text instability is at the 4th-rank NAME, not the 5th: (兼中至) (207×) is emended to (偏中至) (85×) by (寂音) (Juefan Huihong) (以對正中來), which X72n1437 records and rejects as (大悞後學). So (兼中到) as 5th rank should not be confused with the 4th-rank pair (兼中至)／(偏中至).

Senses.PreferredTarget: arriving within togetherness (the fourth of Dongshan's Five Ranks)
AlternateTargets: variant of the fourth-rank name (偏中至)
Senses.Explanation: (兼) both-together / combined + (中) amid, within + (至) arrive, reach: the fourth of the Five Ranks (五位) of the Caodong house. In (洞山良价)'s own (五位君臣頌) the cycle runs (正中偏) → (偏中正) → (正中來) → (兼中至) → (兼中到), the (兼中至) stanza reading "two blades cross points, no need to dodge; a good hand is like a lotus in fire" (兼中至。兩刃交鋒不須避。好手猶如火裏蓮。宛然自有冲天志). The corpus preserves TWO names for this fourth rank. (a) (兼中至) (Zen-scoped 207 hits / 64 texts) is used in Dongshan's (頌) and by later masters — (汾陽善昭) (問如何是兼中至師云意氣不從天地得英雄豈藉四時推), (密雲圓悟) (his own 頌: 兼中至，一棒當頭沒迴避), and the stock (如何是兼中至) catechism (88 hits / 46 texts). (b) (偏中至) (85 hits / 33 texts) is the name in (曹山本寂)'s (五位旨訣), which defines it by the (中孚) hexagram: (偏中至者中孚也)。(隨物不礙)。(木舟中虛虛通自在) (so the 本寂 edition; the 元證 edition punctuates 木舟中虛。虛通自在). The corpus itself records the two names as contested: (覺浪道盛), in his (洞宗標正), writes "'(正來)' and '(偏至)' have been litigated to this day" (正來偏至，聚訟至今) and (乃知偏中至不可以兼中至而重犯兼中到也). The variance runs inside a single master's record: at the identical prose slot (曹山本寂)'s (本寂) edition (T47n1987B) reads (塵中未帶名)。(是曰兼中至) while the (元證) edition (T47n1987A) reads (塵中未帶名)。(是曰偏中至). Both names denote the SAME fourth rank and are distinct from the fifth rank (兼中到) (276 hits / 84 texts; stanza 兼中到。不落有無誰敢和); the form (偏中到) does not occur in the corpus. (覺浪道盛) further glosses "the minister acting as regent" (偏中至者，即臣攝政也). The texts assign the rank no meaning beyond these stated formulations, and neither does this entry.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide sense — a rank name. Origin: (洞山良价)'s (五位君臣頌) (瑞州洞山良价禪師語錄, T47n1986B), which uses (兼中至). (曹山本寂)'s (五位旨訣) (撫州曹山本寂/元證禪師語錄) names the same fourth rank (偏中至) and its self-definition (偏中至者中孚也)… is a X(者)…(也) gloss. (汾陽善昭) (in the 汾陽昭禪師語錄 section of 古尊宿語錄, verified at the cb:mulu) and later masters use (兼中至); (覺浪道盛) (天界覺浪盛禪師語錄, 洞宗標正) uses (偏中至) and documents the (兼)/(偏) dispute. The (元證) (T47n1987A) and (本寂) (T47n1987B) editions of Caoshan's record disagree at the same prose slot — both cited above. Watch the three forms: (兼中至) = (偏中至) (the 4th rank, two names) != (兼中到) (the 5th rank). Counts measured over the 462-text allowlist, main body text (notes/apparatus excluded). Multi-source: Dongshan, Caoshan, Fenyang, Miyun, Juelang; T, C, J canons.

Senses.Explanation: Literally to issue into brightness: to bring something to light or make it clear. The term occurs 1,304 times in 250 allowlisted texts. Chan biographies repeatedly say that someone brings “the great matter,” “the mind-ground,” or “the essentials of mind” to light. One record lists bringing the great matter to light alongside having one's mind-ground opened through mountains and waters and recognizing one's original face through things encountered; the text supplies these neighboring predicates without making them synonyms. A later address states its aim as having each person “directly bring to light one's own fundamental great matter” (直下發明自己本分大事), anchoring direct instruction rather than retrospective biography. Other biographies say “there will certainly be clarification” (必有發明) or that someone was “not greatly clarified” (不大發明). Those result and degree constructions name the outcome of the same bringing-to-light event, not another lexical referent.
Senses.Note: Translate the corpus term rather than importing modern “invention” or automatically making it “enlightenment.” Named-object verbs and result-noun grammar remain one sense. Compare the great matter (大事), fundamental great matter (本分大事), mind-ground (心地), essentials of mind (心要), awakening to the Way (悟道), awakening (悟), and realization (證).
